🦁 Goddess Durga (The Invincible)
Represented in your images [unnamed (14), (15), (38), (42)] as the warrior queen on a lion.

The Root Mantra
"Om Dum Durgayei Namaha"
(Salutations to the Goddess who is difficult to reach and the protector against all evil.)

Quote from the Devi Mahatmayam (The Glory of the Goddess)
"To that Goddess who in all beings is called Power (Shakti), salutations to Her, salutations to Her, salutations to Her, again and again."

Significance: This verse acknowledges that Durga is not just an external deity, but the inner strength residing within every soul to overcome obstacles.

🦢 Goddess Saraswati (The Flowing One)
Represented in your images [unnamed (21), (23)] playing the Veena on a lotus.

The Root Mantra
"Om Aim Saraswatyai Namaha"
(Salutations to the Goddess of wisdom, art, and music.)

Hymn: Saraswati Vandana
"She who is as fair as the jasmine-colored moon, and whose white garland is like frosty dew drops; who is adorned with radiant white attire, on whose arm the Veena rests, and whose throne is a white lotus."

Significance: Saraswati represents the purity of knowledge. "Aim" is her seed (Bija) syllable, believed to sharpen the intellect and the creative voice.

🌺 Goddess Kali (The Dark Mother)
Represented in your images [unnamed (28), (30)] as the fierce blue-skinned deity.

The Root Mantra
"Om Kreem Kalikaye Namaha"
(Salutations to the Goddess who transcends time and brings liberation.)

Quote from the Mahanirvana Tantra
"As all colors disappear into black, so all names and forms disappear into Her. She is the primordial darkness that gives birth to the light."

Significance: Kali is often misunderstood as just "destruction." In reality, she destroys the ego and the concept of linear time, making her the ultimate mother of spiritual liberation.
